strings.name: Guido van Rossum
strings.summary: Guido van Rossum created Python while working at CWI, emphasizing readable and practical programming. He guided its development and later worked at Google, Dropbox and Microsoft. He relinquished the language’s final decision-making role in 2018 and retired again from Microsoft in May 2026.
strings.coverageNote: Sources checked through 13 November 2026; selected milestones extend to 2026, not an exhaustive news record. Institutional achievements are team efforts; announced plans are not completed results.
strings.influence.rationale: Created Python and promoted readable programming and community collaboration, influencing education, research, automation and artificial intelligence.
strings.facts.fact-1.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-2.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-2.value: Mathematics and computer science master’s, University of Amsterdam, 1982
strings.highlights.highlight-1.title: Created Python
strings.highlights.highlight-1.text: Designed and released a language widely used in science, education, automation and software development.
strings.highlights.highlight-2.title: Community and engineering
strings.highlights.highlight-2.text: Led an open-source community and worked on code review, cloud systems and large Python migrations.
strings.timeline.event-1.title: Retired again
strings.timeline.event-1.text: Ended his Microsoft Distinguished Engineer tenure; his résumé now lists retirement.
strings.timeline.event-2.title: C&C Prize
strings.timeline.event-2.text: Received the NEC C&C Prize for contributions to computing and communications.
strings.timeline.event-3.title: Joined Microsoft
strings.timeline.event-3.text: Returned from his first retirement as a Distinguished Engineer.
strings.timeline.event-4.title: Relinquished Python leadership
strings.timeline.event-4.text: Stepped down as BDFL; the community subsequently adopted a new governance system.
strings.timeline.event-5.title: Joined Dropbox
strings.timeline.event-5.text: Worked on mypy and migration of server code from Python 2 to Python 3.
strings.timeline.event-6.title: Joined Google
strings.timeline.event-6.text: Developed code-review tools and worked on App Engine projects.
strings.timeline.event-7.title: Led PythonLabs
strings.timeline.event-7.text: Directed PythonLabs first at BeOpen and then Zope.
strings.timeline.event-8.title: Research in the United States
strings.timeline.event-8.text: Worked at CNRI on Python and distributed systems.
strings.timeline.event-9.title: First public Python release
strings.timeline.event-9.text: Released early Python, gradually establishing an open development community.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Degree and CWI appointment
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Earned his master’s and joined CWI, working on projects including ABC.
strings.timeline.event-11.title: Born in the Netherlands
strings.timeline.event-11.text: Grew up there before later research and engineering work in the United States.
